item.title: La Liga midfielder laments failed Barcelona transfer: ‘It was a dream for me’
item.description: La Liga midfielder laments failed Barcelona transfer: ‘It was a dream for me’ Speaking on Radio MARCA , Racing Santander midfielder Andre Almeida has revealed that Barcelona made an attempt to sign him when he was still at Valencia, only for the club to block the transfer. The 26-year-old Portuguese star is currently on loan at Racing from Valencia for the season, having joined the club last summer. However, if things had turned out differently, he could have become a Barcelona player a few years ago. Almeida claims Barcelona wanted him During the interview, Almeida revealed that Barcelona tried to sign him shortly after he had joined Valencia. The midfielder himself was intent on making the transfer happen, as he saw it as a ‘dream’, but Los Che blocked the move as they were battling relegation at the time. Almeida is currently on loan at Racing Santander. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) “No, no, it was in January, in my first season there, as we were fighting against relegation and I was an important player, and I’d also just arrived at Valencia,” he said. “They wouldn’t let me leave, but obviously it was a dream for me. But you have to accept it when you sign contracts and the club has taken that decision, and I have to accept it.” Almeida signed for Valencia in the summer of 2022, arriving from Vitoria Guimaraes in a deal worth around €8 million. So, going by the player’s statements, the attempt from Barcelona would have come during the January transfer window of 2023, when Xavi Hernandez was in charge of the team. Almeida saw the chance to join Barcelona as a dream. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) However, Valencia proceeded to not sanction the midfielder’s sale as they were fighting for survival in La Liga under former manager Gennaro Gattuso. How has Andre Almeida’s career progressed since then? Having failed to secure his dream move to Barcelona, Almeida remained a regular at Valencia and has gone on to make 119 appearances for the club, registering four goals and 13 assists. Capable of playing in multiple positions, the 26-year-old Portuguese ace moved to Racing Santander on loan in the summer transfer window, where he has played six matches so far. The midfielder was not a part of the Racing Santander squad that lost 7-2 to Barcelona in La Liga earlier this season.

item.title: Thierry Henry stunned by ‘joke’ Jude Bellingham performance as Real Madrid blow Liga title race wide open with Clasico win
item.description: FC Barcelona v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Former Barcelona forward Thierry Henry has heaped praise on Real Madrid following their vital 2-1 El Clasico victory over his old club. The Frenchman was particularly blown away by Jude Bellingham's performance, describing the England international's dominant display in midfield as an absolute joke. Henry praises compact Real Madrid Henry has admitted he was highly impressed by Madrid's tactical setup during their crucial 2-1 El Clasico victory over his former club Barca. Speaking after the weekend's blockbuster fixture, the Frenchman noted that the vital win marked the first time this year he had seen Madrid play in such a compact and resilient manner. According to Henry, Los Blancos were incredibly difficult to beat on the day, conceding very few clear opportunities while remaining highly dangerous on the counter-attack. Despite his natural allegiance to Blaugrana, Henry was quick to acknowledge the impressive nature of the complete performance from the capital club. Bellingham performance was a joke While Kylian Mbappe grabbed the headlines with two goals and the official Man of the Match award, Henry reserved special praise for England international Bellingham. The former Arsenal striker was left entirely in awe of the dynamic midfielder's all-around contribution to the vital victory. Speaking to Betway , Henry explained just how highly he rated the phenomenal individual display. "It was the first time this year that I’ve seen Real Madrid playing like that," Henry noted. "They were compact, not conceding a lot of opportunities, being very difficult to beat and sound on the counter. "Kylian Mbappe scored two goals and was named Man of the Match, but Jude Bellingham? Wow. The way he played reminded me of England’s game in Mexico. He was holding it, turning people, winning a foul, finding a pass or going through himself. I have to give him a lot of credit, the way he played was just a joke." Mourinho answers his critics The vital victory also served as a major statement for manager Mourinho, who had faced external pressure heading into the massive fixture. Henry noted that the jury had been out on whether the renowned coach could still deliver on the biggest stage, but this result firmly proved his enduring tactical qualities. item.title: Nuggets' Aaron Gordon warns Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg that league will humble him
item.description: Nuggets' Aaron Gordon warns Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg that league will humble him originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It has been clear from the get-go that Yaxel Lendeborg was going to play a big part in the Golden State Warriors ' success. During the preseason, head coach Steve Kerr was already talking about how critical he would be to the offense. Lendeborg has taken the reins of the offense when Steph Curry is out or on the bench, but at one point, he was surprised by the opportunity. “Well, it's very shocking to hear it now. But I mean, I get the point. The two other guys are hurt. Jimmy was one of the main scorers on this team. So, going to have to try to fill in his role until he gets back. And I've been in positions where I've had to score the ball a lot, I guess, or an extra amount that I would like. I feel like I'll be able to step into that role for sure. Just got to continue to work at it, get the confidence to do that. But I mean, I feel like everything's going to be trending up the right way," Lendeborg said. The rookie has already faced off against one of the best players in the league, Luka Doncic. Lendeborg made it clear that he lost respect for Doncic after their first NBA matchup. During a recent sit-down with Denver Nuggets forward Aaron Gordon, the NBA champion offered Lendeborg some advice, warning the rookie phenom that the league would humble him. “As far as like your NBA journey, just stay with it. There's some freaks in this League you know what I mean? Like real monsters in this League. This sht will humble you. I thought I was the #1 option in Orlando, not really. Got to Denver, took a couple of steps back, won a championship, improved my game now. Know this League is going to humble you, just always bring that sht, what you learned from, like your mom's, what you learned from the job, bring that, bring that. That's why the Warriors picked you,” Gordon said. Lendeborg is a mature rookie, so when he has a game in which a superstar gets the best of him, he isn't going to let it bother him. Instead, he can use that experience as motivation to improve. The forward has been a great addition for the Warriors, and there is no sign of him slowing down. Gordon's advice was valuable, reminding Lendeborg that he needs to be ready for the challenges that come with playing in the NBA. item.title: Sacramento Kings source shares whether Doug Christie will now be fired after 0-5 start
item.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images The Sacramento Kings have had a dreadful start to the new season, losing each of their first five games. It was always going to be a difficult start for the Kings because of the absence of several key players, but such a poor start has led to calls from many fans for a change of head coach. However, Doug Christie’s seat is set to be safe, for now. Sacramento Kings to stick with Doug Christie despite 0-5 start Even before the Sacramento Kings’ 12-point defeat to the New Orleans Pelicans, there were rumours that Christie’s job was at risk. Many felt the latest loss was the last step and he would be shown the door, especially with fans on social media calling for him to be fired. However, a Kings team source has reportedly told The Athletic that Christie is set to remain in charge and there is no immediate threat to his future. The report claims that ‘there is an internal belief that Christie deserves a fair chance to be evaluated with a team that is much healthier than this current Kings lot’. Ben Simmons, Keegan Murray, Maxime Raynaud and Dylan Cardwell are all currently injured. Simmons has, in fact, been ruled out for the season due to an Achilles tendon tear. The stance on Christie’s future may yet change if the Kings continue losing games at the same rate, but as things stand, there are no plans to part ways with him. Sacramento have two tough games coming up, first against the unbeaten Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday and then against the Dallas Mavericks on Monday. It remains to be seen if the Kings’ stance on Christie will remain the same if they end up losing both of those games. item.title: Patrick Kane Learned How Detroit Still Feels About Him
item.description: Before the Chicago Blackhawks and the Detroit Red Wings dropped the puck Thursday night at Little Caesars Arena, Patrick Kane’s son, Trick, and Alex DeBrincat’s son, Archie, sounded the horn to start the game . Those two families have been close for quite some time. DeBrincat played with Kane in Chicago from 2017-2022 and he also played with him in Detroit from 2023-2026. Kane signed a two-year contract with the Blackhawks in July, and Thursday was the first time he had been back in Detroit since. Oct 29, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Chicago Blackhawks defenseman Artyom Levshunov (55) takes a shot defended by Detroit Red Wings right wing Alex DeBrincat (93) in the first period at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Patrick Kane received a standing ovation from Detroit Red Wings fans in the first period After the first media timeout of the opening period, the Red Wings played a tribute video of Kane’s three seasons in Detroit on the arena video board. Fans stood and gave him an ovation, players on both teams tapped their sticks on the ice, and Kane skated out and saluted the crowd. The tribute came hours after interim general manager Shawn Horcoff announced that forward Dylan Larkin had been suspended without pay, after Larkin’s agent told the team he would not report to the rink. 88❤️ pic.twitter.com/H3LspwqWLM — Detroit Red Wings (@DetroitRedWings) October 30, 2026 Alex DeBrincat comments on Kane returning DeBrincat talked about Kane’s return after the game, in comments published by Red Wings team reporter Jonathan Mills . “It’s always good to see him. I think he was a big part of our team for a couple years there. It sucks that he’s not here anymore, but he’s such a good player. It’s good to see him back in that uniform if he’s not going to be here, so it’s always fun to play against him…He’s a great player.” Detroit won the game 4-1, so the Red Wings got the result and Kane got the reception. DeBrincat and Kane were teammates in two cities, their sons are friends, and the video tribute showed Detroit has not forgotten what Kane did here.

item.title: Fantasy Football Injury Impact: Breece Hall Being A Game-Time Decision Puts Braelon Allen's Value In Question
item.description: New York Jets running back Breece Hall (20) warms up during a preseason opening game between the New York Jets and Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Friday, Aug. 14, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect New York Jets running back Breece Hall once again failed to get in a full practice this week after practicing in a limited capacity on Friday. He is listed as questionable for Week 8 when the Jets host the Las Vegas Raiders and will likely end up being a game-time decision. This is a situation you'll have to monitor right up until inactives are released about 90 minutes before the game's 1:00 PM EST start time. Breece Hall (quadriceps) will be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders. Via @BrianCoz pic.twitter.com/pjF8Jx7cph - RotoWire Fantasy Football (@RotoWireNFL) October 30, 2026 Fantasy Impact RB Breece Hall, New York Jets We never expected Hall to play last week, but there is a real chance he suits up this week. However, it could be risky for his long-term health if he hasn't been able to get in a full practice yet. Everyone saw what happened with Saquon Barkley last week after rushing back from a soft tissue injury. Like hamstrings, a quad injury can be tricky and is prone to re-aggravation. Braelon Allen playing so well in Hall's absence also allows Hall to take his time in returning, which is a nice luxury for the Jets. This one could go either way, but if Hall is active, you should be starting him. This is a situation to monitor closely leading up to Sunday's game. RB Braelon Allen, New York Jets Allen has looked great with Hall sidelined, and there are a ton of fantasy owners who would love to see Hall take one more week to get healthy. If you own both Hall and Allen, you are probably better off with just Allen playing as well. He has done well enough to carve out a potentially significant role in the offense even when Hall returns. However, if Hall is active, we would probably bench Allen this week until we get a good look at this backfield with everyone healthy. If Hall is out, Allen is a great start against the Raiders, who are allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to running backs this season. Bowen twisted his ankle earlier in the week and required treatment, but returned to training ahead of the game. “Jarrod twisted his ankle in training,” Nuno said. “He had treatment for a couple of days, but he joined us today, and he seems okay.” There was also a positive update on Konstantinos Mavropanos, whose knee injury is not as serious as initially feared. “It’s his knee,” Nuno said. “We were concerned about his injury but thank god it’s not as serious as expected and he’s recovering quite well. “Let’s see how long it takes. He was on the grass today by himself so it’s positive in some ways. “We were afraid it was going to take longer but I think soon he’s going to be good.”

item.title: Arteta warns Dowman 'we are not in Disneyland' after red card
item.description: Mikel Arteta had words with Max Dowman after the teenager was sent off [Getty Images] Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has told Max Dowman "we are not in Disneyland" and that he intends to hold the teenager to the same standards as other first-team players. Dowman, 16, was sent off in the 85th minute of Arsenal's penalty shoot-out loss to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday after reacting to a heavy challenge by Harrison Neal and will serve a three-match ban . A visibly annoyed Arteta spoke to Dowman as the teenager left the pitch, and on Friday spoke about the incident for the first time, saying he warned the attacker before the game about dealing with provocation. "I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it is positive or negative. But you need to understand the context and the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out," Arteta said of his words to Dowman. "But, I don't know. You can have another reaction. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me some days you might say 'I don't like the reaction'. For me, it was the best reaction to be who I am." Arteta revealed that he had spoken to Dowman on Thursday and said there were "no issues at all" between the pair. However, he added that he needs to be "very straight" with Dowman and clear of the standards expected. Dowman was sent off for the England U19s earlier this month where he was also on the end of heavy challenges in a match with the United States. Of that red card, Arteta said: "They are his age. They are 16 – the same. What is the reaction? That is the level and that is the reaction. "And whether it is right or wrong, that is the reaction." Arteta also spoke of the impact the red card had on the team, saying: "And the reaction when I don't win, you want to know what my reaction is? I am [angry] big time. "So, we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality, otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League and this level. "We look after him so much that you cannot imagine. "But at the same time we are going to demand from him, like everybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Because the other boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair." The Gunners did appeal against the red card but the Football Association (FA) upheld the decision. Of that, Arteta said he was "very disappointed", adding "we are lucky today that he (Dowman) hasn't had a broken foot." The English manager is under severe pressure after a run of two wins in 12 games across all competitions this season. The poor form has seen the team drop down to 16th in the Premier League table after eight games. The Red Devils have already exited the EFL Cup and have lost two of their three games in the Champions League. The situation has added to speculation over Carrick’s future, with several candidates mentioned as his possible replacement. However, the Belgian midfielder, who joined United from Aston Villa this summer, has thrown his weight behind the English manager. Carrick’s role in Tielemans’ Old Trafford move Speaking to TNT Sports , Tielemans explained why the United squad want Carrick to continue at the Theatre of Dreams. The Belgian said: “I came here partly because of him, because he wanted me here. He wanted me to help the team out.” “So I’m very happy for him to stay, and the whole group, we don’t want a sudden change. We don’t want a big change that is going to disrupt things more than they are. We just need stability, we need to keep working hard, and it’s going to turn at some point.” Tielemans went on to insist that the entire squad is backing the English manager, adding: “Since I’ve come in, he’s always done his work. He’s tried to put a system in place that we all feel comfortable in. I joined this summer, because he convinced me to come over and help the team out.” “I can only speak positively about him, and everyone in the changing room would do the same. item.title: Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark announces he will step down in January
item.description: Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark announces he will step down in January originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormack will be stepping down from his role in January 2027. ESPN's Pete Thamel announced the news Friday. He is leaving to pursue a career outside of college sports. “When I accepted this job, my goal was to put this conference on an upward trajectory and truly believe that the future of the conference could not be in better shape,” Yormack said. “The next commissioner of this league will inherit a conference that is ’16 Strong.’ There has never been a better time to be a member of the Big 12 than right now.” Yormack took the reins as Big 12 commissioner in 2022, shortly after Texas and Oklahoma packed their bags for the SEC. He succeeded Bob Bowlsby and helped the conference land a new TV deal with Fox and ESPN. "I think in all fairness, had he not joined us and convinced us to go early on redoing our television deal, we all believe we could have ended up like the Pac-12 did," Kansas Chancellor and Big 12 Board Chair Doug Girod said about Yormack, per ESPN . "We certainly recognized that and believed it at the time. As it played out, it demonstrated it was the right move. His leadership, experience and networking in the media world have continued to be extremely beneficial for us." Yormack led the way through a major conference realignment, welcoming eight new schools. He took advantage of the PAC-12 divorce by adding Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah. “I am looking forward to passing the baton to the next commissioner and continuing to cheer this league on as a lifelong fan of the Big 12,” Yormack told On3’s Brett McMurphy. The Big 12 extended Yormack’s contract through the 2030 college football season, according to ESPN . “When I accepted this job, my goal was to put this conference on an upward trajectory and truly believe that the future of the conference could not be in better shape,” said Yormark. “The next commissioner of this league will inherit a conference that is ’16 Strong.’ There has never been a better time to be a member of the Big 12 than right now.” In his four years as commissioner, Yormack did things the untraditional way by landing deals with companies like Monster Energy Drinks and other sponsorship and marketing agreements. Girod said Yormack was everything the Big 12 was looking for because he was not a traditional athletic director but was innovative and aggressive in bettering the conference. item.description: Micho ahead of S04RBL: "Heading to Schalke full of self-belief" RB Leipzig face their next challenge in the Bundesliga away at promoted side FC Schalke 04 on Saturday at 15:30 CET. Ahead of the game, head coach Martín Demichelis spoke to the media about which players are unavailable and how his side will approach the game. Read on for all the key quotes from today's pre-match press conference. The opponent "We've done our analysis of Schalke and we're expecting a team that play with aggression. They don't create many chances, but they also don't concede many goals . Their style of play is what got them promoted and they've continued to stick to it. The most important thing will be how we approach the game. We need to be smart . The game in Essen is a good example: even with ten men, we were courageous both in and out of possession . We now need to do exactly that again. We took a step forward against Essen. It's the first time that we've managed to come back in a game that we've trailed in, and so we're heading to Schalke full of self-belief. " Fitness after the mid-week games "We're fit. Once again, the game three days ago is the best example of this. There are no excuses to not run . For me, it was important for us to rotate the squad against Elversberg . That allows us to be ready to take the game to our opponents even in when we play in midweek. We had 22 healthy outfield players in training today, so we have the option to rotate." item.title: Wrestling legends loved Christian Watson’s WWE-style return to Packers-Panthers
item.description: What Christian Watson pulled off in the Week 8 game between the Green Bay Packers and Carolina Panthers was nothing short of a WWE -like storyline. Watson exited the contest in the second quarter with a chest injury and was even forced to make a trip to the hospital for further testing on his injury. At that point, we thought Watson’s night was over because who could possibly expect the Packers wideout to return to a game after all of that. However, we were dead wrong, as Watson came back to the stadium one quarter later, and not only did he return to the contest, he received a target immediately. MORE: NFL trade deadline tracker – Grades for every deal, list of available players If you’ve watched professional wrestling over the years, you’ve seen plenty of ambulance entrances and exits, so Watson’s return had a very WWE-style feel to it. WWE legends react to Watson’s return Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson (9) during the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) WWE legend and Hall of Famer Triple H shared his reaction to Watson emerging from the ambulance to return to the game. The only thing missing, Triple H said, was entrance music. “This isn’t a video game… you did that!!! Next time we’ll work on getting you some entrance music,” Triple H said when getting wind of Watson’s postgame comments about his return. Fellow WWE Hall of Famer Paul Heyman revealed that the origin of the ambulance entrance was in 1991 in WCW, when the now-defunct company did something similar with Sting. MORE: Josh Jacobs assigns blame for ‘handcuff’ TD celebration And, we’re not clear if he’s joking, but Heyman said football is “pre-determined.” “We did this with (Sting) in 1991 in WCW (vs Ravishing Rick Rude), and the industry has repeated it with great success in numerous circumstances,” Heyman said. “My most sincere compliments to the (NFL) creative team. Nicely Done… I love football. Even though it’s pre-determined,” Heyman added. Christian Watson sees WWE parallel Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson (9) reacts after making a catch against the Carolina Panthers at Lambeau Field. Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) After the game, even Watson admitted he felt like he was in a scene from a WWE show. “I used to watch WWE as a kid,” Watson said. I felt like I was watching WWE Smackdown vs. Raw or something, seeing the cameras on me when I was coming out of the ambulance.” Watson went on to note that the trip to the hospital was spurred on by the fact that he was spitting out blood after his injury . However, everything checked out, which allowed him to make his epic return to the field. Watson finished the game with eight receptions for 113 yards, with two of those catches and 13 of those yards coming after his return. The Packers went on to win the game, 27-19, and improved to 5-3 on the season. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trend

item.title: Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark to leave conference
item.description: Big 12 Commissioner Brett Yormark speaks at the Big 12 NCAA college football media days in Frisco, Texas, Tuesday, July 8, 2025. (AP Photo/LM Otero) (LM Otero/Associated Press) Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark is leaving the conference, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported on Friday. Yormark, who has been with the Big 12 since 2022, is expected to accept a new role outside of college sports. He'll be with the league at least through January of 2027. Yormark's background before coming to the Big 12 was outside of the college realm with jobs in entertainment, television and pro sports. Yormark replaced Bob Bowlsby in 2022 and, after declaring the Big 12 "open for business" was instrumental in a new six-year, $2.28 billion television deal with Fox and ESPN and the transition of four new schools - Houston, UCF, BYU and Cincinnati – that agreed to join before his arrival after Texas and Oklahoma announced plans to move to the SEC. Yormark was also successful in luring Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah from the Pac-12 in 2023. This is a developing story and will be updated. item.description: Would you buy it? Italian club unveils a kit inspired by a… sweet! 😯 Having played in Italy's top flight in the 2025/2026 season, Cremonese have made a poor start to the current Serie B campaign. And they are "banking" on a new look to turn things around, sitting just 15th after nine rounds. Founded in 1913, Unione Sportiva Cremonese hail from Cremona, a city in the Lombardy region. The city is famous for, among other things, torrone, a sweet made with egg whites, honey, sugar and nuts (peanuts, almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts or pistachios). And that very delicacy was the inspiration behind Cremonese's fourth kit. How about this video? The kit launch could only have taken place in one location: a torrone factory. Cremona's pride in being known as the "City of Torrone" takes center stage on the shirt. Cremonese reached nine points in the second division after beating Catanzaro last Tuesday (27). They return to action this Saturday (31), hosting Benevento at 11 a.m. (Brasília time). Palermo lead Serie B with 23 points. Sampdoria, meanwhile, are struggling in 19th and second-to-last place with just five. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: 4 keys to a Lions victory over the Vikings in Week 8
item.description: Jan 5, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (26) runs with the ball in front of Minnesota Vikings safety Camryn Bynum (24) and scores a touchdown during the second half at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Detroit Lions (4-2) and Minnesota Vikings (6-0) will meet in Week 8 in an NFC North divisional clash. The Vikings are the last remaining undefeated team in the NFL, and while their defense is playing at an elite level, they’ve yet to face an offense like the Lions, making this a fantastic strength-on-strength showdown. “Minnesota is playing outstanding football,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said earlier in the week. “(Head coach) Kevin (O’Connell)‘s doing a hell of a job. (Defensive coordinator) Brian (Flores) is doing a hell of a job. This thing, they play very complementary football. […] I’ve got a lot of respect for this team, the way they play, but we’re looking forward to this; this will be good.” Let’s take a closer look at this matchup and predict how the Lions will earn a victory over the Vikings in this week’s Honolulu Blueprint. This week’s prediction preview is sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , who currently have the Lions listed at +1800 to win this year’s Super Bowl and are currently 3.5-point favorites in Week 8 . Viking s base scheme For a detailed look at the opposing scheme, check out our complementary breakdown piece: Lions Week 8 preview: Breaking down the Vikings’ offensive and defensive schemes . Prediction 1: Counter creativity with creativity The Vikings enter this game undefeated, but outside of their NFC North games against the Packers and Bears, their opponents have been bottom-of-the-league teams, totaling seven wins and 20 losses combined. Now, they’re headed into the toughest part of their schedule, beginning with the Lions’ elite offense—the first top-10 DVOA offense they’ve faced this season. The Vikings’ success is built almost entirely on their defense, which ranks in the top 10 in virtually every meaningful defensive statistic and is top one or two in most of them. Over six games, they’ve suffocated teams with their aggressiveness (their 69% blitz rate is over 20% higher than the next-closest team), and with a veteran unit that returns most of its starters, they rarely make mistakes. I go into more detail in my breakdown of the Vikings defense in the article link above, but at their core, the Vikings are so problematic because of their creative blitzing and quarters zone coverage. On most traditional downs, the Vikings will deploy a base 3-4 defense and line up seven or eight defenders in the box and then “double mug” blitz them, meaning bring an overloaded pressure on a single side of the offensive line or straight up the middle (double A-gap). The goal is to disguise where the blitz will come from and gain an extra blitzer in one area, while unexpectedly dropping players into coverage in the opposite area.

I go into more detail in my breakdown of the Vikings defense in the article link above, but at their core, the Vikings are so problematic because of their creative blitzing and quarters zone coverage. On most traditional downs, the Vikings will deploy a base 3-4 defense and line up seven or eight defenders in the box and then “double mug” blitz them, meaning bring an overloaded pressure on a single side of the offensive line or straight up the middle (double A-gap). The goal is to disguise where the blitz will come from and gain an extra blitzer in one area, while unexpectedly dropping players into coverage in the opposite area. The Vikings are so efficient at disguising their intentions and getting to the quarterback quickly that they lead the NFL in pressures on 49% of pass-rushing attempts, 21 sacks, and a 10% sack rate. While the Vikings are operating at a scary level, it’s not a defense that is unfamiliar to the Lions and quarterback Jared Goff. In previous seasons, Goff has done well to manage the blitz, especially when he has a healthy offensive line. In games where Goff has succeeded, he’s found creative ways to offset the Vikings’ creativity, and his ability to stay calm under duress— he’s currently the best quarterback in the NFL vs. the blitz, with an EPA of 0.32 —has led to success in the six games this season. Here’s an excerpt from NextGenStats’ game insights: “Jared Goff has been sacked once and completed 15 of 19 passes for 162 yards and three touchdowns across 20 max blitzes faced this season (i.e., 6 or more pass rushers), resulting in a career-high 78.9% completion percentage. [….] Goff has faced a max blitz on at least six dropbacks in each of his past six meetings with the Vikings during the Brian Flores era dating back to 2023, a threshold he has reached in just three of 51 other games played over that span.” In recent weeks, purposefully or not, we’ve already seen the Lions testing some concepts to beat an overloaded blitz. Concepts like spreading out five wide, or shifting a tight end into the backfield in a fullback role, will help the Lions offense create quick outlets or adjust their protection. The Lions have also sprinkled in some 21 personnel (two running backs and one tight end), where Sione Vaki stays in to protect, allowing Jahmyr Gibbs to be an outlet for Goff’s passing game. While the Lions will need to be creative with their running backs and tight ends, their receivers will likely help Goff produce downfield. Last week, we saw the Lions deploy Amon-Ra St. Brown more on the outside, and he caught seven of his nine targets for 109 yards against the Packers. Expect more of that in this game, as the Lions will want to get St. Brown isolated vs. the Vikings’ zone, giving him more space to operate. Also, it wouldn’t be surprising to see them give St. Brown some choice routes, where he can adjust the depth based on who the Vikings blitz. As NextGenStats also pointed out, the Lions have also found a separation advantage by lining up St.Brown and Jameson Williams on the same side of the formation: “The Lions’ passing offense has been more explosive when they align to the same side through seven weeks, as they have averaged 8.0 yards per play with a 18.3% explosive-play rate on those snaps.” By pairing them, Williams can stretch the zone deep and force the defensive backs to adjust to his speed, opening things underneath for St. Brown. If the defense takes the underneath route, then they’ll have to try and stick with Williams one-on-one deep. With the Vikings’ philosophy of limiting explosive plays, look for the Lions to stress their zone and take what they have underneath. The Lions offense vs. the Vikings defense may be the NFL’s premier matchup this week. item.description: Blue Jays predicted to sign $32M two-time Cy Young winner, 2x All-Star to form duo with Dylan Cease originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Blue Jays are coming off a very disappointing 2026 season in which they missed the playoffs after reaching the World Series in 2025. This offseason will be another critical one as they look to make some major additions. The thing about Toronto is that it needs healthy pitchers. This winter will be all about finding the right guys. “Some injuries, you can see coming. When the 42-year-old Max Scherzer runs into a few IL stints, no one should be surprised. When José Berríos has Tommy John surgery after not missing a start for nearly a decade, it's terribly unfortunate, but we all understand the realities of baseball and the limitations of the human elbow. The Blue Jays are trying to find that line now between bad luck and controllable variables," MLB.com's Keegan Matheson wrote. The Blue Jays' pitching staff could look very different next season, but this is what their rotation is expected to look like to begin the year. “So, as long as Cody Ponce is healthy when Opening Day comes around, they will be running a four-man rotation as is: Dylan Cease, Trey Yesavage, Jose Soriano, and Cody Ponce. Eventually, the team will welcome back Jose Berrios, but it has been a rough go of things in terms of his health," SI's Maddy Dickens wrote. However, CBS Sports' Mike Axisa believes Toronto could make a major move by signing Tarik Skubal this winter. “Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He showed few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract,” Axisa wrote. That would be the move of the offseason for Toronto if the Blue Jays could convince him not to re-sign with the Los Angeles Dodgers . Ultimately, it will come down to Skubal's preference and what happens during the MLB lockout. Skubal played on a $32 million contract this past season. Toronto wants to get back to the World Series, and landing the best starting pitcher in the league would be a great place to start. item.title: INTERVIEW: Bayern Munich's Phillip Lahm reflects on his highs and lows facing Borussia Dortmund
item.description: INTERVIEW: Bayern Munich's Phillip Lahm reflects on his highs and lows facing Borussia Dortmund MÜNCHEN ( Bulinews ) ahead of FC Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund's clash tomorrow , Phillip Lahm reflected on some of his career highs and lows from his experiences of Der Klassiker. "Around 2011 and 2012, that is my worst recollection [of playing against Dortmund]," the former Bayern captain said during a media round at the club's Säbener Straße training ground attended by Bulinews.com . "We were playing away in Dortmund four games before the end of the season [in 2012]," Lahm explained, with the two rivals separated by just three points going into their hotly-anticipated Matchday 29 meeting. "We played quite well but then we had the missed penalty [by Arjen Robben and lost 1-0]. And that's why the championship was lost. We also lost the DFB-Pokal final 5-2 [to BVB], that was not good either. "But I also have some really good memories of [successful DFB-Pokal] cup finals against Dortmund as well. Of course the Champions League final [Bayern won 2-1 against Dortmund] in 2013 as well. "After the time when we didn't manage to become German champions in 2011 and 2012 [losing to Dortmund in both], we managed to win the 2013 DFB Supercup in Dortmund [at the Signal Iduna Park]. "This was so important for our self-awareness ahead of the coming season. Because before this, Dortmund became Bundesliga champions and the cup final that we lost 5-2," Lahm concluded. The versatile full-back – who made over 517 appearances for the Bavarians – remained tight-lipped on what he expects to happen this Saturday. However, one would naturally expect him to be rooting for his boys in Red.

item.title: Iraola glad to raise Liverpool fans' hopes but says hard work ahead
item.description: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola (Paul Currie) Andoni Iraola is pleased his side's performances have left some Liverpool fans dreaming of a Premier League title challenge ahead of Sunday's match at home to champions Arsenal, even if it is too soon for him to pay much attention to the table. Victory at Anfield would see Liverpool move to within three points of Arsenal, who are currently level at the top of the table with leaders Manchester City. Liverpool are on a five-game winning run in all competitions, a sure sign of their progress as they adapt to the methods of former Bournemouth manager Iraola in his first season on Merseyside since replacing the sacked Arne Slot. But Iraola said Friday: "It is still October. We have to take one game at a time and I always say the reference is more or less when we've played against each other once so halfway through the season. That's when you can start to look at the standings. "Right now, we are in a position where we need to improve and keep getting better." But asked if he welcomed the increasingly buoyant mood among Liverpool fans, the Spaniard replied: "For fans, it is good if they have expectations or they think we can win." Arsenal moved level with City at the top of the table following a 2-0 win over Everton last weekend, but then suffered a huge upset defeat on Tuesday after being knocked out of the League Cup on penalties by fourth-tier Fleetwood. "We know Arsenal and how good they are," Iraola said. "They have very good players, working a lot in synchronicity and we have to be ready for that challenge. "It's going to be a demanding game but we also trust our players, trust ourselves and in the good atmosphere we will for sure have on Sunday. I hope we will be at a level to win this game." As for Liverpool's recent run, a cautious Iraola said: "It is five wins (in a row) but just two are in the league so if we are talking about the league we still need more wins to recover points. "But definitely we know what we want in terms of we have to improve a lot of things. But, if you can do this process while you are getting results, it is always nice." jdg/nf

item.description: Born in London and spending his formative years in Nigeria, Osi Umenyiora had never even heard of American football until he moved to the U.S. as a teenager. After moving to Auburn, Alabama, he took up the sport in high school and eventually earned an opportunity at Troy University. He was drafted by the New York Giants in 2003 and went on to win Super Bowls XLII and XLVI. Umenyiora spent ten years with the Giants and two seasons with the Atlanta Falcons before retiring in 2015. The rest, as they say, is history. Yet Umenyiora's story was far from over. How can I now give this opportunity to more people?'" That's where an e-mail to NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell snowballed into NFL Africa, the league's initiative to grow the game on the continent and perhaps Umenyiora's most impactful chapter yet. It's something that I'll never forget and something that I cherish. Courtesy of Osi Umenyiora How did that time there shape you into who you are today? Umenyiora: In a multitude of ways. The environment there teaches you how to survive first and foremost. It instills toughness. There are so many things that you see there that, whenever you leave that environment, the ability to thrive in those situations, you can carry them with you pretty much anywhere. I know they say that if you can make it in New York, you can make it anywhere, but really, it's if you can make it in Lagos, Nigeria, you can pretty much make it anywhere. Courtesy of Osi Umenyiora Names can carry so much weight in African culture. What’s your full Nigerian name and what does it translate to? Umenyiora: Ogemdi Ositadinma Iloabuchi Umenyiora . My father would actually name us after periods in his life. So Ogemdi means 'My time is now'. Ositadinma means, 'From today, things will be good', and Iloabuchi basically means, 'The heart of who is God'. So it's three different names. Then one of [my dad's] friends went to him and was like, 'You have four sons at this point, and none of them are named after you. Why don't you name one of your sons after you?' So he just started calling me Osi randomly when I was two years old and that's how I got the name. But my first name is actually Ogemdi. How do you think the meaning of your name has played out in your life? Umenyiora: First and foremost, just understanding that my father would name all his children — and he had ten of them — after different periods of his life. I think it was a very special and sentimental thing for us because a lot of times you don't really know the meaning of your names, or people just randomly call their children whatever. But the fact that my father took the time to think about each one of his children and specifically name us after something that happened translates, and it just gives your name that much more pride and that much more meaning. Also, the thing about Nigerian names is you can tell where somebody's from within Nigeria just by hearing their name, which is kind of unique to a lot of people. So I can hear somebody's name, and I'll be like, 'Okay, this guy is Fulani, or he's Hausa, Yoruba, or Igbo, simply by hearing their name. The name really is an identifier. It's a marker of who you are, where you come from, and a lot of times it actually carries your whole family history with you. Courtesy of Osi Umenyiora You are Igbo. Can you talk about the values and traditions that come from your culture that have led to your success on and off the field? Umenyiora: Being from the Igbo tribe, we're very, very proud people. Obviously, there was a situation back in the '60s and '70s where Nigeria fought a war. Biafra was trying to secede from Nigeria. It didn't work out well, but the Igbo people were the main people who were in that. So, just being a part of that tribe, I would say I find it interesting how I don't really consider myself Igbo until I get to Nigeria. Because outside of Nigeria, you're just Nigerian. Everybody is cool. They're family. You're just one. But the minute you go back into Nigeria, that's when you become either Igbo, Hausa, Yoruba, Fulani, Ijaw, Efik, Ibibio — one of those tribes. To be honest, I wish that we would take more of the approach that we have outside of Nigeria into Nigeria, so we can be more cohesive and really move as one within the country. Because outside of the country, my best friends are Yoruba, Hausa, it doesn't really matter until you go back in. I wish we would stop that. You are a two-time Super Bowl champion, a New York Giants legend. So much of your journey was shaped by hard work and values, but your journey is also a testament to the power of having someone believe in you and take a chance on you. How has that inspired this chapter of your life as the lead for NFL Africa? Umenyiora: Oh, massively! A lot of times, people can look at things that they do and things that they accomplish and think that they're the ones who did it. For me, I've never thought that way. I always knew that I was very fortunate. I was lucky to have the parents that I did who were able to send me to America. I was lucky to be able to start playing the game of football, which gave me the opportunity to get a scholarship and then go on to the NFL. My whole story has just been one of pure fortune, and so I looked at it like, 'Okay, I've been given this opportunity, and now I'm working with the NFL. How can I now give this opportunity to more people?' Because there are so many people, especially when I was growing up, who were more talented than me, had much more ability than me, but they just didn't have the parents, or they didn't have the [opportunities]. So now that I'm in a position to help, why would I not try to put those people in the exact same position that I'm in? As opposed to just going back there and doing the regular things. 'Oh, we're going to do a charity here. We're going to do this and that.' Cool. I get all that, but for me, it was about this: There are tremendous athletes there. There are people there with real ability, and all they need is just a pathway. All they need is just somebody to hold the door open for them, so they can come and make the best of their abilities. For me, the idea that I had this opportunity to do something like that, given the fact that I was given that exact same opportunity, was monumental, and it's something that I knew that I had to do. Jackson has scored seven goals for Aston Villa since joining from Chelsea at the end of August. His double in Villa’s 2-1 win over Manchester City, and his former manager Enzo Maresca, last weekend, to end their 100 per cent record , took him to six goals in his last six appearances for Unai Emery ’s side, including four in four in the Premier League. He has become the leading man in the new-look attack that is Emery’s Villa 2.0, ensuring the departure of Ollie Watkins, who Villa sold to Al Hilal for £50m, has largely gone forgotten. He is doing everything Emery wants from his striker: pressing from the front, running the channels, and, yes, being clinical in the box when the chances arrive. goodnight, villans pic.twitter.com/YT46ScjsEo — Aston Villa (@AstonVilla) September 19, 2026 That it comes as a surprise that Jackson has suddenly found an eye for goal is perhaps unfair, but it is a reputation that was forged, of course, by his previous two-year spell in the Premier League at Chelsea. Jackson was 22 when he was signed by the ensemble of Chelsea’s various sporting directors for £32m, as part of a transfer policy designed to bet on youth and potential. He arrived as a relative novice, following a season at Villarreal where he had played less than half of the minutes available to him at LaLiga. Scoring 17 goals in 44 appearances under Mauricio Pochettino in his first season in English football was, on reflection, a decent return, but Jackson became defined more by the opportunities he didn’t take than the ones he did. Rightly or wrongly, a narrative set in: Jackson was willing but raw, wasteful and, at times, ill-disciplined (managing to pick up eight yellow cards before Christmas in his first season is some achievement, but it added to the frustration). Jackson’s underperformance on xG (expected goals) also became a stick to beat him with. The Senegal international had the fifth-highest xG in the Premier League in his first season, with 18.7, but scored just 14 goals. After Chelsea sacked Pochettino that summer the pattern continued under Maresca, scoring 10 goals from 12.3 xG. By the time Jackson was sent off in a crucial away game at Newcastle for elbowing Sven Botman, patience was already wearing thin. It felt as if it had run out completely when Jackson was sent off again during that summer’s Club World Cup. Jackson’s final Premier League appearance for Chelsea was a sending off against Newcastle (Getty) Eventually, Jackson seemed to be dragged down by the focus on what he was not doing – not converting enough chances – rather than being lifted up and encouraged by what he was – which was getting those chances in the first place. Only five players (Erling Haaland, Mohamed Salah, Alexander Isak, Watkins and Cole Palmer) registered more xG than Jackson during his previous two seasons in the Premier League, and Jackson was not even taking penalties. Landing on the conclusion that Jackson was a poor finisher seemed to rule out the possibility that he could, one day, deliver the goals he was expected to if he worked on his shooting and sharpened his instincts in the box. What he needed was a little time, a little care, a little space to grow up. He was not going to find that in the constant churn at Chelsea, although they may argue selling Jackson to Villa for a huge profit, in a deal that could reach £65m, was a successful piece of business. Profit and financial return is not, though, what football should be about. At Aston Villa, Jackson has reunited with a manager in Emery who gave him his first break at Villarreal five years ago, but a coach whose relentless energy appears to derive from demanding hard work and driving improvements in his players at every opportunity. Emery looked at Jackson and saw a player who was already an ideal fit for his system, but could jump to another level if he slowed down in the box and developed that dead-eye finishing that defines the elite. “His challenge has been when he can have chances to score, always [aim] in the corner of the goals, because he was shooting so much at the beginning of the season like in rugby,” Emery told TNT Sports following Jackson’s brace against City, mimicking with his hand a skyward shot that was blazed over the posts. “So he is progressing as well.” Unai Emery joked Jackson’s finishing at the start of the season was like a rugby goal-kicker (Getty) It was, in truth, a bit of a dig, but delivered in the classic Emery way that meant it came from a supporter, as well. He also enthused about Jackson’s all-round impact. “How he was working, how he was defending, how he was getting duels – wow,” said a coach who is not often prone to hyperbole. The challenge now, of course, is continuing that, and sustaining what is actually now a pattern of overperformance following four Premier League goals from 1.84 xG since he arrived at Villa. These are early days, but the look Jackson is firing down the TV cameras confirms that he has indeed read your takes and kept the receipts from two years ago. In the eyes of Premier League fans, he has been the one to be written off. Now it’s Jackson’s turn to be judge, jury and executioner. The outstretched thumb is hanging horizontally, and you’d better hope it doesn’t end up pointing down.

Do you know who that is?” Lee then replied, “Are you referring to Son Heung-min?” Jeong went on: “So it appears to be true. … It has also been revealed that the national team’s leadership is causing discord and has broken down overall.” Lee declined to comment. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
